- jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs: +42 re-exports (28 from bead description matched source exactly; +14 additional types found: PushSubscriptionCreateInput/Patch, SpacePatch, Blob types, Quota).
- jmap-calendars-client/src/lib.rs: +3 (AddedItem, SessionClient, SetError) — local input/response structs were already re-exported.
- jmap-tasks-client/src/lib.rs: +2 (AddedItem, SetError) — no local method-arg/response structs; only standard infra missing.

Gates clean: cargo check --workspace, cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check. No public-API removals; purely additive.
description:
Per workspace canonical-template rule (jmap-mail-client AGENTS.md), every extension-client sibling must mirror the canonical's shape modulo only spec content. jmap-mail-client/src/lib.rs re-exports input parameter structs (EmailGetParams, MailboxSetParams, EmailSubmissionSetParams, EmailImportInput, EmailParseParams, EmailCopyParams) at the crate root.

jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs (lines 32-36) re-exports only response types (AddedItem, ChangesResponse, GetResponse, Patch, PushSubscriptionCreateResponse, QueryChangesResponse, QueryResponse, SessionClient, SetError, SetResponse, SpaceJoinResponse, TypingResponse). The chat-client input parameter structs (ChatCreateInput, ChatPatch, ChatQueryInput, MessageCreateInput, MessagePatch, MessageQueryInput, ReactionChange, SpaceCreateInput, SpaceQueryInput, SpaceJoinInput, AddMemberInput, UpdateMemberRoleInput, SpaceAddMemberInput, SpaceUpdateMemberInput, SpaceAddChannelInput, SpaceUpdateChannelInput, SpaceAddRoleInput, SpaceUpdateRoleInput, SpaceAddCategoryInput, SpaceUpdateCategoryInput, CustomEmojiCreateInput, CustomEmojiQueryInput, SpaceInviteCreateInput, SpaceBanCreateInput, ChatContactPatch, ChatContactQueryInput, PresenceStatusPatch, ContactSortProperty) are reachable only via jmap_chat_client::methods::X.

Discovered while writing JMAP-uuoi.3 wiremock smoke tests — every test had to write the long jmap_chat_client::methods::FooInput path rather than the canonical's flat jmap_mail_client::FooInput shape.

Related: jmap-chat-client's input structs are #[non_exhaustive] while the canonical's are not. That is a separate divergence (visible at construction time, not at import time) and is out of scope for this bead.

Scope of fix:
1. Add the input parameter structs to the pub use list in crate-jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs.
2. Audit the other 5 extension-client siblings (calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing) for the same divergence and propagate the fix.

Acceptance:
- jmap_chat_client::ChatCreateInput etc. work without the methods:: path
- Per canonical-template rule, every sibling extension-client crate re-exports its input structs at lib root
- No public API removed; this is additive

Spotted while completing JMAP-uuoi.3 (chat-client wiremock smoke tests).
notes:
Audit complete 2026-05-10: every extension-client sibling diverges from the canonical (jmap-mail-client) to a different degree. Map:

  Canonical mail-client (lib.rs:25-30): re-exports 7+ input/output param structs:
    EmailCopyParams, EmailGetParams, EmailImportCreated, EmailImportInput,
    EmailParseParams, EmailParseResponse, EmailSubmissionSetParams, MailboxSetParams,
    plus AddedItem/ChangesResponse/GetResponse/QueryChangesResponse/QueryResponse/
    SessionClient/SetError/SetResponse.

  calendars-client: re-exports 1 input struct (CalendarEventGetParams) + response types.
  contacts-client:  re-exports 1 input struct (AddressBookSetParams) + response types.
  filenode-client:  re-exports 3 input structs (FileNodeCopyParams, FileNodeOnExists,
                    FileNodeSetParams) + response types.
  sharing-client:   re-exports 0 input structs (only response types).
  tasks-client:     re-exports 0 input structs (only response types).
  chat-client:      re-exports 0 input structs (only response types, plus SSE/WS items).

Scope expansion: this is not chat-client-only — every sibling needs its input parameter structs lifted to lib root to match the canonical. The propagation rule (workspace AGENTS.md Canonical Templates) requires the propagation pass.

The mail-client canonical AGENTS.md banner specifically calls this out:
'If you change this crate, propagate the change to every extension-client
sibling in the same pass (or file a follow-up sweep bead before merging).'

Suggested decomposition: one child bead per sibling crate. Canonical is the
target shape (re-export every public *Input / *Patch / *Params / *Response
type from methods at lib root). Each sibling bead identifies the
crate-specific input struct list (e.g. chat-client's 27+ input structs
listed in this bead's original description).

Also note: chat-client's input structs are #[non_exhaustive] while the
canonical's are not. Constructing them from outside the crate requires
::default() + field assignment rather than struct literals (visible in
crate-jmap-chat-client/tests/chat_smoke_tests.rs:173-176). That is a
separate divergence axis.


[Sequencing question for human, filed per workspace AGENTS.md 'Turn questions into beads' rule]

This bead has grown beyond a single chat-client fix into a 6-crate cookie-cutter sweep. Three plausible paths:

(a) Convert this bead to an epic and file 6 child beads (one per sibling crate), with chat-client (or sharing/tasks, which are tied for worst divergence) as a canonical-shape decision point first.

(b) Land all 6 fixes in one large coordinated commit ('refactor(*-client): lift input parameter structs to lib root for canonical-template consistency'). Smaller blast radius per commit, but the fix is purely additive (re-export only — no public type removed) so the risk of a single combined commit is low.

(c) Defer entirely: argue that since the mail-client canonical itself only crystallized recently, full propagation can wait until the canonical's shape is stable.

Recommendation: option (a) — file as epic, propagate per sibling, but use one short PR per sibling so review can scope each crate's full new lib.rs export surface independently. Mail-client should NOT be touched in this sweep; it's the oracle.

Until human triages: this bead remains labeled 'human'. Other do-beads sessions should skip it (the labeling rule).
